title: Working · guard, haul and rescue
blurb: The heavy end of the species: sled dogs, mountain rescue dogs, water dogs and the guarding breeds that were built to hold a gate.

items.d: Chukchi sled dog from north-east Siberia: 20–27 kg, built for distance in the cold, and a talker.
The heavy freighting dog of Alaska's Inuit: 34–43 kg, slower than a husky and far stronger.
Alpine rescue dog of the hospice pass: 64–120 kg, with a famous nose for snowbound travellers.
Canadian water dog with webbed feet and an oily coat, bred to haul nets and rescue swimmers.
The German giant, 71–81 cm at the shoulder, once a boar hound and now a gentle house dog.
German butcher's drover and guard dog: stocky, confident and protective of its people.
Created in Thuringia in the 1890s as a guard and companion: lean, alert and quick to learn.
German bull-baiting descendant turned family guard: 55–70 cm, playful and stubborn.
